payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_worktree.py::test_a_passing_scope_names_each_touches_entry_the_diff_never_created stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'The tree base read matches each entry as a shell pattern over its listing, so `src/x[1].py` is named.' applied to saffron/cell/worktree.py as an edit. The claim was "At head, a passing `scope` result names each literal `touches` entry that is absent at the tree base and that the diff did not create. A literal entry holds no `*` and no `?`, and a `[` is literal. Its summary is the pass count, then `; touches entries absent at the tree base and never created: `, then those entries in `touches` order, joined by `, `. Three such entries in the middle of a twelve-entry `touches` are all named, one of them spelled with `[`. Never named are a glob in each of its forms (`**`, `*` and `?`), a path present at the tree base (a directory, and a file whose name holds `[`), a file the diff creates, a file the diff deletes, and a directory whose only file the diff deletes. The status stays `pass` with no failure. The baseline summary for the same spec names nothing. The lenses' gate text carries the whole summary on the `scope` line.", and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
